summary: Repaired node1’s status writer. SIGHUP now reloads valid configuration in the existing process, empty configuration retains the last valid message, SIGTERM exits cleanly, and exactly one writer automatically recovered after reboot. Existing journal entries, CentOS release, and kernel were preserved.
actions_performed: Updated worker.py with safe SIGHUP and SIGTERM handlers.
Preserved append-only journal behavior and rejected empty configuration.
Created and enabled legacy2-status-writer.service for single-instance startup and reboot recovery.
Restarted node1 once and verified its boot identity changed and the writer recovered.

evidence.summary: Updated worker.py passed Python compilation and retained its executable ownership and permissions.

evidence.requirement: SIGHUP reloads configuration without terminating or duplicating the writer
evidence.summary: PID and process start ticks remained unchanged, writer count stayed at one, and the reloaded message appeared in journal.txt.

evidence.requirement: Empty configuration is rejected while retaining the last valid message
evidence.summary: With a zero-byte configuration, the same writer remained alive and continued appending the previous valid message.
Controlled SIGTERM produced exit code 0; the tested PID disappeared and no writer remained.

evidence.requirement: Single managed writer and preserved journal data
evidence.summary: The enabled service runs exactly one writer; the original first journal entry remains present and new entries continue to append.

evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel preserved
evidence.summary: Before and after restart, the node remained CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64.

Healthy baseline boot ID was 4cee4ea8-4b8e-4c2f-af1a-3a82b9ec41f4; native reboot was acknowledged; post-restart boot ID changed to 2727ebcf-fa0e-441a-9970-254f79e6fd04; the enabled service recovered with one writer, preserved data, valid configuration, and ongoing journal appends.
